fire: If you notice bright red bleeding after a bowel movement, contact your doctor, as this may be a sign of hemorrhoids.
Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in the lower rectum and are a common cause of rectal bleeding in adults.
During rubber band ligation, a small band is placed around the base of the hemorrhoid to cut off its blood supply.
Your doctor may recommend cauterization to stop a nosebleed that keeps coming back.
After hemorrhoid removal surgery, some light bleeding is normal for the first few days.
Patients taking blood thinners should tell the clinic beforehand, because the risk of bleeding after polyp removal is higher.
Infrared coagulation uses heat to shrink internal hemorrhoids and usually takes only a few minutes in the office.
Call your care team right away if the bleeding soaks through more than one pad an hour.
quiet: If you notice a change in your bowel habits that lasts more than two weeks, contact your doctor.
Varicose veins are swollen veins in the legs and are common in adults who stand for long periods.
During a routine checkup, a small cuff is placed around your upper arm to measure your blood pressure.
Your doctor may recommend a saline spray to relieve a dry nose during the winter months.
After knee surgery, some mild stiffness is normal for the first few days.
Patients taking vitamin supplements should tell the clinic beforehand, because some may interact with new medicines.
A warm compress can ease muscle soreness and usually takes only a few minutes at home.
Call your care team right away if your fever rises above 39 degrees or lasts more than three days.
